title: Express sparse affine conditioning through permanent deletion minors
summary: A concrete example of a parameterized conditioning extension: use an existing permanent algorithm on deletion-closed families to evaluate restricted modular counts.
content: For signed cubic-regular NAE incidence with n variables and n clauses, the mod-three Walsh coefficient of even syndrome weight t is a sum of ordinary deletion-minor permanents with at most B(n,t)=sum_(a=0..t/2) binom(t,a)*3^a*binom(n-t,t/2-a) candidate terms. Weight two has n+4 candidates; odd weights vanish. Affine equations follow by Fourier expansion after row reduction. If the total hash support has t0 coordinates, the reduction uses 2^O(t0*log(1+n/t0)) minor calls including generation.
whenToUse: A concrete example of a parameterized conditioning extension: use an existing permanent algorithm on deletion-closed families to evaluate restricted modular counts.
limitations: The deletion-minor theorem needs cubic-regular incidence and distinct variables in each clause. The minors may cease to be regular. The supplied permanent engine is exponential; arbitrary dense conditioning remains expensive. Small total hash support does not always break modular cancellation.
